6.speaker: Lucian Galade
6.text: "Most people find the Supreme Court's absolute authority over constitutional changes dangerous. Look at the situation we currently have, Mr. President. The Judiciary has power over every branch."

7.speaker: Nia Morgna
7.text: "We will be ensuring that there won't be another politically motivated Supreme Court."

8.speaker: Lucian Galade
8.text: "If we can fully reach an agreement with the reformists, we will be very strong in the Assembly to propose the change."

10.speaker: Nia Morgna
10.text: "Yes. This will ensure that there won't be another politically motivated Supreme Court."

11.speaker: Petr Vectern
11.text: "That's why the Old Guard have bargaining chips over us."

12.speaker: Lucian Galade
12.text: "We can't just bribe the Old Guards. Judge Garaci and the Chief Justice Hawker will do their best to undermine us."

13.speaker: Nia Morgna
13.text: "Most of them won't. But we already talked about my vote and a possible agreement with Isabel which may change things."

14.speaker: Lucian Galade
14.text: "Now we have a better picture of your intentions, sir. I will start reaching out to my contacts to make a draft that works for us."

15.speaker: Petr Vectern
15.text: "Well, regardless of what Mr. Rayne decides, we will need to work together to push this agenda."

16.speaker: Nia Morgna
16.text: "I'll present your input to the committee. In a few months, you would have the draft on your desk to make the final changes yourself."

22.speaker: Nia Morgna
22.text: "We'll need to break the power of the Old Guard within USP first. Most of the conservative wing are still loyal to their Colonel."

23.speaker: Lucian Galade
23.text: "Now we should wrap this up. Since we evaluated the points, I'd like to hear your input, sir."

25.speaker: Nia Morgna
25.text: "This is yet another point that was unanimously agreed on by all parties. Tarquin Soll established this rule to protect his '29 Constitution. We all know most of the judges are still his pawns."

26.speaker: Player
26.text: "I won't support these reforms. We'll work with the Old Guard to block them."

27.speaker: Player
27.text: "Can we reach a two-thirds majority in the Assembly?"

30.speaker: Nia Morgna
30.text: "Even though Mr. Ricter put on a whole show about why vetoes should completely be removed, the committee has almost unanimously agreed on fixing the loopholes, thus limiting presidential vetoes."

31.speaker: Player
31.text: "Is it possible to pass the Supreme Court?"

33.speaker: Player
33.text: "I'm sure the rest can be bribed."

34.speaker: Lucian Galade
34.text: "If you can get Frens Ricter to work with you on this, our only problem would be uniting our own party. We'll never be able to get NFP to work with us."

35.speaker: Nia Morgna
35.text: "Apart from these two critical points they have other major demands."

37.speaker: Player
37.text: "Who else would be willing to support reforms?"

38.speaker: Lucian Galade
38.text: "They are the biggest obstacle. Even if we pass the Assembly, the Chief Justice will do his best to block our amendments."

39.speaker: Player
39.text: "So, we only have 3 votes out of 11?"

40.speaker: Nia Morgna
40.text: "They want to reform the appointment procedures of the ministers. Mr. Ricter clarified that the Assembly should have a say in the formation of the council of ministers."

44.speaker: Nia Morgna
44.text: "Well, Mr. Ricter also talked about abolishing the Member of Honor rights of Tarquin Soll that gives him absolute immunity and makes him a permanent member of the Assembly."

45.speaker: Petr Vectern
45.text: "That is something that a majority in our party also supports."

46.speaker: Petr Vectern
46.text: "I'm sure it's possible. But regardless of my opinion, we *need* to persuade most of them to support us for passing an amendment to the Constitution."

48.speaker: Petr Vectern
48.text: "Well... That one is a controversial one. I doubt that USP would like that."

49.speaker: Petr Vectern
49.text: "The conservatives have around 40 seats. There are many unaligned people and some of your "loyalists" might decide to show their true faces too."

50.speaker: Lucian Galade
50.text: "Immunity of the Justices, the impeachment of the president, limiting the power of the presidential decrees... All of this came up during the committee meetings."

51.speaker: Player
51.text: "Do you think they can be persuaded?"

52.speaker: Nia Morgna
52.text: "Yes, reformists expect big reforms while our faction in the USP are not very keen on pushing changes that are too great."

53.speaker: Player
53.text: "We did it before for the elections. We can do it again."

54.speaker: Petr Vectern
54.text: "I'd say keeping everything in the middle ground is the safest bet. No need to agitate anyone too much."

56.speaker: Player
56.text: "I disagree. We'll push for comprehensive reforms."

57.speaker: Lucian Galade
57.text: "But we might try and bribe the centrists of the Court. I think we might get Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin with a bribe. The toughest will be Mrs. Edmonds."

58.speaker: Player
58.text: "I agree. Let's keep the changes small and manageable."

59.speaker: Nia Morgna
59.text: "Two of the judges are friends of mine, and of similar opinion about the reforms. Consider them with me."

60.speaker: Player
60.text: "They have valid concerns that we need to look at."

61.speaker: Petr Vectern
61.text: "We should reach out to the judges in secret. Some of them might be willing to break rank to support us."

62.speaker: Nia Morgna
62.text: "I'm with you on this, Mr. President."

63.speaker: Lucian Galade
63.text: "We need at least 6 of the 11 judges to vote for the proposal. But Mr. Hawker has enormous influence over the judges."

64.speaker: Nia Morgna
64.text: "As long as we address the main issues, I also agree."

66.speaker: Nia Morgna
66.text: "I'll keep working with them and keep you updated, Mr. President."

67.speaker: Lucian Galade
67.text: "But it will be tough to unite the USP with all the divisive wings that have formed. You must make them follow you loyally."

68.speaker: Lucian Galade
68.text: "We need the majority of our 130 seats in the Assembly to vote in favour. With PFJP's full support of 70 votes, we will easily surpass the needed 166."

70.speaker: Player
70.text: "They will not be allowed to dictate the negotiations."

71.speaker: Petr Vectern
71.text: "Albin Clavin and his reformist wing would be supporting you. He already weighed in heavily in the committee meetings."

72.speaker: Nia Morgna
72.text: "Constitutional amendments will still be very difficult to accomplish with a reform like this, particularly because we will keep the two-thirds vote system to be able to propose a change. However, the judiciary will not have the final say in the amendments."

73.speaker: Nia Morgna
73.text: "I think Judge Edmonds can be persuaded. And in extension, Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin."

74.speaker: Player
74.text: "This is already what we wanted to do."

75.speaker: Petr Vectern
75.text: "However, the conservatives would be tough to break. The influence of Soll is still living strong in the party."

77.speaker: Nia Morgna
77.text: "They weren't really blinded by the Sollist ideology."

78.speaker: Player
78.text: "And what good does that do to us?"

79.speaker: Nia Morgna
79.text: "Three votes, yes. But I believe that Judge Edmonds can be persuaded as well. She and two other judges, Mr. Dalton and Mr. Martin."

80.speaker: Lucian Galade
80.text: "We'll go through each of the main demands of the committee, and get your input. Mrs. Morgna can explain them further."

81.speaker: Player
81.text: "The loopholes give the President too much power."

82.speaker: Lucian Galade
82.text: "We'll start with the first *red line*. The new Constitution will fix the loopholes regarding the president's absolute veto powers."

83.speaker: Player
83.text: "We need the Court to even pass this change. Why would they support this?"

85.speaker: Nia Morgna
85.text: "My suggestion is to add a clause detailing the methods the Assembly may override a veto with some sort of a super-majority. One person should never be able to block the rest."

86.speaker: Petr Vectern
86.text: "So we need as many of the conservatives to support us. And there is only one person who is key to make them back us."

88.speaker: Player
88.text: "They will surely support a just cause for the country and its future."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "All means are to be considered in order to succeed."

91.speaker: Narrator
91.text: Nia was taken aback by the statement.

92.speaker: Lucian Galade
92.text: "The second one is about the judiciary. The new Constitution will remove the Supreme Court's right to vote on legislation."

93.speaker: Petr Vectern
93.text: "And there is only one person who is key to make them back us."

94.speaker: Nia Morgna
94.text: "According to the Constitution, I am a member of the Supreme Court, which means we already have one vote."

96.speaker: Lucian Galade
96.text: "We should run-down each of the main demands of the committee, and get your input first. Mrs. Morgna can explain them further."

97.speaker: Petr Vectern
97.text: "I don't think this is up to discussion for any reformists."

98.speaker: Nia Morgna
98.text: "I also have reasons to think she might be in Orso's pocket. She will be tough to break, but we'll need her help to get the conservative support."

99.speaker: Petr Vectern
99.text: "Yes, those three don't seem to be working directly with the Chief Justice Hawker. If we can get to Isabel Edmonds, we might get the 6 votes needed. That's our best bet."

100.speaker: Petr Vectern
100.text: "Yes, we'll need to talk to Judge Edmonds. If we can get to her, we might get the 6 votes needed. That's our best bet."

101.speaker: Player
101.text: "I stand in agreement with Mr. Ricter. The vetoes should be removed."

102.speaker: Petr Vectern
102.text: "This is one of the starting points of the whole discussion about changing the constitution."

103.speaker: Nia Morgna
103.text: "Whatever you decide it's important to get a balanced picture. We will be making history by changing the '29 Constitution of Soll."

104.speaker: Petr Vectern
104.text: "Most of their support is necessary to be able to amend the Constitution. And there is only one person who is key to make them back us."

106.speaker: Nia Morgna
106.text: "Gloria Tory. She's well respected by the Sollists. She'll be our biggest obstacle in the Assembly and her demands will be extensive."
